```{python}
#| echo: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads((Path(".") / "opengwasdb_chunk_comparison_benchmark.json").read_text())
configs = {c["name"]: c for c in data["configs"]}
BASE, NEW = "1000x1000", "1000x128"

def md_table(headers, rows):
    sep = "|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(headers)) + "|"
    head = "| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |"
    body = "\n".join("| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in r) + " |" for r in rows)
    return f"{head}\n{sep}\n{body}"

def fmt_ms(v):
    return f"{v:,.1f} ms" if v < 1000 else f"{v/1000:,.2f} s"

def timings(name):
    return {t["query"]: t for t in configs[name]["timings"]}
```

## Overview

Both stores hold the **same** genome-wide ukb-b data — 2,514 UK Biobank GWAS ×
~9.85M variants — and differ only in the zarr **chunk shape**. The baseline uses
square `1000×1000` chunks; the variant keeps the 1,000-variant rows but narrows
the analysis axis to **128**. An identical query selection (the same ALIDs,
analysis ids, and region) is run against each store.

The point of interest is the **per-analysis (`bulk`) read**. With a
1,000-analysis-wide chunk, reading one analysis column drags in 999 neighbours
per chunk; a 128-wide chunk cuts that waste ~8×. The per-variant (`phewas`) read
moves the other way — it now spans more analysis-chunks — so this is a trade, and
the table shows both sides.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
d = data["dataset"]
rows = [
    ("Analyses (GWAS)", f"{d['n_analyses']:,}"),
    ("Variants (hg38)", f"{d['n_variants']:,}"),
    ("Repetitions (median of)", data["reps"]),
    ("Baseline chunks", "×".join(map(str, configs[BASE]["chunks"]))),
    ("Variant chunks", "×".join(map(str, configs[NEW]["chunks"]))),
]
print(md_table(["Property", "Value"], rows))
```

## Query latency: 1000×1000 vs 1000×128

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
DESC = {
    "bulk": "One analysis, all variants (`analysis`)",
    "phewas": "One variant × all analyses (`phewas`)",
    "regional": "All associations in a 1 Mb window (`range_phewas`)",
    "tophits": "Genome-wide significant index read (`top_hits`)",
    "random_lookup": "100 variants × 10 analyses (`lookup`)",
}
tb, tn = timings(BASE), timings(NEW)
rows = []
for q in DESC:
    b, n = tb[q]["median_ms"], tn[q]["median_ms"]
    speedup = b / n if n else float("nan")
    tag = f"**{speedup:.1f}× faster**" if speedup >= 1.05 else (
        f"{1/speedup:.1f}× slower" if speedup <= 0.95 else "≈ same")
    rows.append((DESC[q], fmt_ms(b), fmt_ms(n), tag))
print(md_table(["Query", "1000×1000", "1000×128", "Change (128 vs 1000)"], rows))
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Median query latency by pattern (log scale). Lower is better."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

order = ["bulk", "phewas", "regional", "tophits", "random_lookup"]
labels = ["bulk", "phewas", "regional", "tophits", "lookup"]
tb, tn = timings(BASE), timings(NEW)
base = np.array([tb[q]["median_ms"] for q in order])
new = np.array([tn[q]["median_ms"] for q in order])

C_BASE, C_NEW = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834"
x = np.arange(len(order)); w = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 4.6))
b1 = ax.bar(x - w/2, base, w, label="1000×1000", color=C_BASE)
b2 = ax.bar(x + w/2, new, w, label="1000×128", color=C_NEW)
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(
    lambda v, _: (f"{v:g} ms" if v < 1000 else f"{v/1000:g} s")))
ax.set_ylabel("median latency (log scale)")
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e3e2da", lw=0.7, which="major")
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
for bars, vals in ((b1, base), (b2, new)):
    for rect, v in zip(bars, vals, strict=True):
        txt = f"{v:.0f} ms" if v < 1000 else f"{v/1000:.1f} s"
        ax.annotate(txt, (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width()/2, v), ha="center",
                    va="bottom", fontsize=8, color="#555")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Storage

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
rows = [
    ("1000×1000", f"{configs[BASE]['store_gb']:,.1f} GB"),
    ("1000×128", f"{configs[NEW]['store_gb']:,.1f} GB"),
]
print(md_table(["Chunk shape", "Store size"], rows))
print()
print("Chunk shape changes how the same float16 `z`/`se` are grouped on disk, so "
      "compressed size shifts only modestly; the point of the narrower analysis "
      "chunk is read amplification on per-analysis queries, not storage.")
```

---

## Takeaway

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
tb, tn = timings(BASE), timings(NEW)
def ratio(q):  # >1 means 1000x128 is faster
    return tb[q]["median_ms"] / tn[q]["median_ms"]
bulk_abs = (tb["bulk"]["median_ms"] - tn["bulk"]["median_ms"]) / 1000
print(f"- **`bulk` (per-analysis) is {ratio('bulk'):.1f}× faster** at 1000×128 "
      f"({tb['bulk']['median_ms']/1000:.1f} s → {tn['bulk']['median_ms']/1000:.1f} s, "
      f"−{bulk_abs:.0f} s) — the chunk-bound read that dominated the square layout.")
print(f"- **`phewas` and `random_lookup` are slower** ({1/ratio('phewas'):.1f}× and "
      f"{1/ratio('random_lookup'):.1f}×): both gather variant rows across more, narrower "
      f"analysis-chunks. `phewas` stays in the millisecond range; `random_lookup` pays "
      f"~{(tn['random_lookup']['median_ms']-tb['random_lookup']['median_ms'])/1000:.1f} s.")
print("- `regional` and `tophits` are chunk-insensitive (variant-range scan and "
      "index-served read).")
print()
print("The trade is a large absolute win on the per-analysis read against a "
      "sub-second-to-second cost on per-variant point reads. 1000×128 is the right "
      "default when bulk / per-GWAS export dominates; keep the square chunk if random "
      "point-lookups and PheWAS latency are the priority.")
```
